author: NorthEast News Desk
body: JPMorgan Chase ended lending activity for Situational Awareness after leveraged bets tied to artificial intelligence produced large losses and brought the hedge fund close to collapse, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. The fund liquidated most of its public-equity holdings to Citadel after a global rout in chip stocks exposed the scale of its borrowing.

Situational Awareness was launched in 2024 by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner and built concentrated positions across the AI ecosystem. The fund told investors its portfolio fell 67% in July, when the selloff generated a margin call and pressure to raise capital or dispose of holdings. JPMorgan was one of its key lenders before notifying the fund that the relationship would end.

Other banks, including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Bank of America, remain active brokers for the fund, and it recently began working with Clear Street. The episode illustrates how leverage can amplify a crowded technology trade when markets reverse. Reuters said the banks declined to comment and Situational Awareness did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
dek: The bank ended its lending relationship after leveraged artificial-intelligence bets produced steep losses, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.
headline: JPMorgan curbs lending to AI-focused Situational Awareness fund
